section_summary.extract_value: This Results section reports moderation analyses testing whether attachment to God (anxiety and avoidance) moderates the negative associations between three types of social comparison (body, eating, exercise) and body appreciation in a single study sample. Overall, more frequent social comparisons were associated with lower body appreciation, and these relationships were conditional primarily on God attachment anxiety (and, for exercise comparisons, also on avoidance); three separate moderation models were run. No explicit study numbering (e.g., 'Study 1') is used in the section.
section_summary.evidence_source: Each of the social comparison dimensions (that is, body, eating, and exercise) was tested separately; hence, a total of three moderation analyses were performed.

section_summary.extract_value: This section reports results for a single, unnamed study of women (descriptive N = 186; regression analyses use N = 164). Body mass index was inversely related to body appreciation (r = -0.30), and moderation analyses showed that God attachment anxiety (and in some cases avoidance) moderated the negative association between social comparison (body, eating, exercise) and body appreciation.

section_summary.extract_value: This section reports results from moderation analyses examining how God attachment anxiety and avoidance moderate relationships between three types of social comparison (body, eating, exercise) and body appreciation in a female sample. Body, eating, and exercise comparisons were each inversely related to body appreciation, with these effects generally stronger at higher levels of attachment anxiety; exercise comparisons showed moderation by both anxiety and avoidance. Figures 1–3 and regression tables (Notes: N = 186; Notes: N = 164) are referenced, and sample-size inconsistency is present between reported notes.
